name: São Paulo/Guarulhos–Governor André Franco Montoro International Airport
before:
Brazil's biggest airport sits in Guarulhos, a municipality on São Paulo's north-eastern edge, and it handles more passengers, more aircraft movements and more cargo than anywhere else in the country. Locals still call it Cumbica, after the district and the air force base that shares part of the site. The formal name honours André Franco Montoro, a former governor of São Paulo state, and has done since 2001. In 2012 it was rebranded as GRU Airport and handed to a private consortium to run.

Most UK travellers meet it as a gateway rather than a destination: it is the main international door to São Paulo and a major connecting point for onward flights across Brazil and the rest of Latin America. Traffic is heavy enough that operations are capped at 45 an hour, one of only five Brazilian airports with slot restrictions, so schedules tend to be tightly managed.

Its reputation is built on punctuality rather than glamour. Aviation analysts have repeatedly ranked it among the world's most reliable large airports, and it has been picked out as a sensible place to sit out a long layover.
after:
Brazil's busiest airport, in the Cumbica district of Guarulhos, about 25 km from central São Paulo. It handled more than 47 million passengers in 2025, 16.8 million of them on international flights. An air force base shares the airfield. The formal name honours André Franco Montoro, a former governor of São Paulo state, and has done since 2001. Since 2012 it has been run under a private concession, as GRU Airport.

It is one of the main hubs in Latin America, and British Airways flies here from Heathrow. ANAC, the regulator, lists it as one of four Brazilian airports where it allocates take-off and landing slots.

Its reputation is built on punctuality rather than glamour. The aviation data firms OAG and Cirium have repeatedly ranked it among the world's most punctual large airports.

claims.note: Was 'Brazil's biggest airport'. In 2025 it retook first place in all of Latin America (operator, via Panrotas), and Aena, which runs Galeão, calls Galeão the country's second air gateway behind only Guarulhos.

'More than 47 million' is true of both.

claims.claim: British Airways flies here from Heathrow
claims.inAfter: British Airways flies here from Heathrow
claims.note: New, in place of 'Most UK travellers meet it as a gateway rather than a destination', which no source supports. BA's own page sells London to São Paulo (fares shown to February 2027, 11 hours 40 minutes); the operator's live airline list has British Airways at Terminal 3; the UK CAA's 2025 route table shows 517,683 scheduled passengers between Heathrow and São Paulo Guarulhos (and none from any other UK airport except a few charter passengers in 2024). LATAM also flies London to São Paulo on older sources, but LATAM's own sites refused automated reads (403, 'for security reasons'), so it is not named.

quote: Our cheapest flights to Sao Paulo from London

claims.claim: one of four Brazilian airports where ANAC allocates slots
claims.inAfter: ANAC, the regulator, lists it as one of four Brazilian airports where it allocates take-off and landing slots.
claims.note: Was 'one of only five Brazilian airports with slot restrictions'. ANAC's slot page lists four coordinated airports today (Congonhas, Guarulhos, Recife, Santos Dumont); its capacity-declaration page (updated 13 June 2025) lists the same four, and Brasília is now only a 'facilitated' airport. Wikipedia's five (with Brasília and Pampulha) is out of date: ANAC's open-data folder for Pampulha's summer 2026 slots is empty. Attributed to ANAC because only ANAC's own pages give the current count.

quote: Atualmente a ANAC é responsável pela coordenação de quatro aeroportos no Brasil:
A ANAC desempenha o papel de coordenador responsável pela alocação de slots nos aeroportos coordenados do Brasil.

claims.claim: repeatedly ranked among the world's most punctual large airports
claims.inAfter: The aviation data firms OAG and Cirium have repeatedly ranked it among the world's most punctual large airports.
claims.note: Was 'most reliable'; the rankings measure punctuality. OAG placed it third among large airports (operator, in its 2015 to 2016 timeline) and second in 2017 (Wikipedia); Cirium's June 2024 report placed it second of all airports and fourth among large airports. Wikipedia's 'first among large airports in 2024' is not what the cited Cirium report says (Congonhas was first), so no single ranking is quoted. Cirium's 2025 awards do not name Guarulhos. In review (23 Sep), 'Aviation analysts' was replaced by the two firms' names, OAG and Cirium, so the text says who ranked it.

sources.quote: GRU Airport foi ranqueado pela OAG, maior empresa de banco de dados da indústria da aviação, como o terceiro mais pontual no mundo em pousos e decolagens, dentro da categoria de grandes aeroportos.

quote: THE ON-TIME PERFORMANCE MONTHLY REPORT - AIRPORTS JUNE 2024

sources.quote: In 2017, it was considered by the company OAG the second best in punctuality in the world and first in Latin America
